questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to experience a different culture compared to the Danish one.
I thought that Italy was a good choice based on my starting point of wanting to experience something different. They have a different culture and they have good food. 
I also thought it would be a good place to improve my English

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I received a lot of mails from host university, but I think a lot of the information came quite late compared to when I needed the information.
I had to find a lot of the information that I needed by myself, but I got the mobility/exchange e-mail from my host university and wrote to them a lot.
So the information should have been easier to find then you have to find it yourself. And the university should have send out information earlier than they did.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I did not get any physical assistance probably due to covid.
But the university were good at answering emails with useful answers, but sometimes it took a little long.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found housing together with another student from my home university so I think we might have had more options. But it was hard to find housing, because it is expensive to live on Venice island if you want to live close to campus.
We found our apartment through airbnb, but we also looked in different housing in Venice groups on facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If future exchange students want to live off campus they should become members of facebook groups about housing in Venice. They should begin looking well in advance.
Or they could try to contact the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
First I had to get access to the online student area of my host university. I did this by using a step-by-step guide I received by e-mail together with my student number and code
The second thing I had to do was make a study plan through a function in the online student area where I add the courses from my pre-approval. To do this I also followed a step-by-step guide I received in another e-mail.
The last step was to add the courses on the moodle page and get the rest of the information for the course there and in class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails with information and different step-by-step guides for each step of the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I was able to register for all of my classes with  the step-by-step guides 
I was even able to change a course during the semester as the course changed the language from English to Italien.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
My advice would be to just follow the step-by-step guides you receive by mail and you must be patient as the mail comes kind of late.
And if the students experience difficulties they should just write to the university

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took both courses at both BA and MA levels. 
I would say that most of the courses were at the expected level, which I expected to be a little bit lower than at KU. But it is hard to say since I had both kinds of levels and I don't really thought about the difference in levels while I was there.
I also had some courses were some of the topics of the course syllabus I had already had in courses at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I think the biggest difference between the teaching was the form of the examination. At KU most of the exams are on a computer with closed books. In Venice, the exams are written by hand, but also with closed books.
The style of the teaching I think it is kind of the same as at KU. We had lectures where the professors reviewed the most relevant from the syllabus and then there was also time to do excises on our own and there were also some assignments to do during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Behavioural Economics
Financial Economics
Labour Economics
Economics of Inequality
Advanced Management of Nonprofit Organizations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would just recommend to choose courses that are on the economics department in Venice. One of the courses (corporate finance) i choose was in Treviso which is a city right next to Venice, but you would have to take the train as it is another campus and the courses changed from English to Italien as all of the other students were Italien and I think that students who attends that campus are Italiens and not exchange students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had hoped to visit other cities in Italy, but I didn't know how many I would have time for

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had expected that food would be expensive, but eating at restaurants was more expensive than I thought. But on the other hand, the drinks were less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was different kind of sports activities as I received emails about football and rugby.
The cultural and social activities it was mostly offered by the Erasmus organization which were trips to other cities as well as trips to some of the Vendian Islands. 
The university had a few aperitivo (food and drinks) nights in the end of the semester, but it was only advertised for in their own canteen

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To go on the trips that the Erasmus team organized. They go to a lot of nice places both in Venice, and also other cities. It is also a good way to meet other students and get new friends

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
They should go see the st. Marco square and some of the many churches in Venice and just walk around the city without a GPS.
They should also visit Burano, Murano, and some of the Vendian Islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was easy to adjust, but I also lived with another exchange student from KU so we encouraged each other to go out and so on.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the campus and other social activities they have. Talk with students in the classes. And get a welcome buddy which the university offers at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe they are way more open and whereas Danes are more reserved and reticent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the Italians' helpfulness and openness as well as their food and social life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go to the welcome activities and other social activities in the beginning to make friends 
- Be patient - in general, things are a little slower than in Denmark, both in shops and at university. The university is a little bit low to give information and answer your questions, but answers will come and they don't ignore you.
- Enjoy the city and don't forget to have fun and experience Italy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have mentioned the most relevant

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friendships and acquaintances I made and being allowed to experience and hear about other cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not all Italians are good at English so sometimes you have to be imaginative

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
